slides.notes: Persona 1 is the lead persona. It targets the buyer who is already halfway to the close, so the ad's job is arithmetic, not persuasion.
Four buyers, four different reasons for stalling. One campaign has to speak to the average of them, which is nobody.
July sold a discount to strangers. September sells a landowner an argument about the thing they already own, and only then hands them the money.
This buyer is already halfway to the close. The message asks them to reappraise an asset they already hold, which is arithmetic rather than aspiration.
Card one never says a dollar amount. Land is the hook, the qualifier, and the thing no competitor can answer.
The value of the land counts toward the build.
This buyer has taste and a budget. What they lack is confidence that a custom build stays under control.
Sells governance, not creativity. This buyer is not short on taste, they are short on confidence that a custom build stays under control.
This buyer did not decide against building. They called a bank, heard what a construction loan involves, and quietly stopped.
This buyer did not decide against building. They called a bank, heard what a construction loan involves, and quietly stopped. This persona does not sell a house, it removes a bank.
This person has been saving photographs of this house for years. Showing them one more beautiful room does nothing.
This person has been saving photographs of this house for years. Showing them one more beautiful room does nothing. What they are missing is a date.
